findings.evidence: RaiMapsToRanged: 'if (raw != KiteStance || !g_cfg.rangedRules) return 0; if (!g_cfg.kiteApproach || !ebp) return 1;' while a failed frame read returns 0 (line 351). So ebp=0 yields 1 (stance maps to vanilla Ranged, no approach) even with a melee weapon or an out-of-range target, but an unreadable live frame yields 0 (Aggressive approach). RangedAI.h:32-33 documents the return as 'under current weapon/range conditions' and says ebp=0 is a stance-only check.
findings.suggested_investigation: Find the MapsToRanged consumer (companion_ai_src A1 hook, per RangedAI.h:4-6) and check which ebp it passes when no frame is available. Decide whether ebp=0 should return the weapon/range answer or 0, and make the unreadable-frame and ebp=0 paths agree. Then check whether the common contract test's fake provider (common_contract_test.cpp:221) is the only thing exercising this rule.
findings.why_it_matters: kite_approach exists because Ranged's no-approach rule re-queued attacks forever for melee or out-of-range party members (E-H3 comment, lines 327-330). A public-API caller that passes ebp=0 (the documented stance-only path) gets the no-approach answer and reintroduces that stall. The two failure paths also disagree.

findings.evidence: KPatchInit: 'if (api && api->struct_size >= offsetof(KPatchApi, require) + sizeof(api->require) && api->provide) { api->provide(K2RAI_IFACE, K2RAI_VERSION, &g_raiApi); }'. The size guard is computed from the require field, but the code dereferences and calls provide. The HudHost.h guard pattern (require-only check) is the same, so this is only safe if provide sits before require in KPatchApi.
findings.suggested_investigation: Locate struct KPatchApi in kpatch_api.h (Common, outside this packet; not found under _shared_src) and compare offsetof(KPatchApi, provide) with offsetof(KPatchApi, require). If provide comes later, guard on offsetof(provide) + sizeof(provide) instead.
findings.why_it_matters: If provide is declared after require in kpatch_api.h, an older patcher whose struct_size covers require but not provide makes this read past struct_size, which is a bad read inside the game process at init.
